sources.title: ENDGAME editorial principles agreed in the website project
sources.text: Personal strategy starts by identifying the owner's own objective. GOAL -> POSITION -> MOVE -> OUTCOME. Clarify the goal and accepted trade-offs. Map company needs, other shareholders' stated interests, actual decision rights and dependencies. Develop an executable route plus a genuine alternative. Track progress against the personal objective and the business conditions that support it. The owner cannot silently override others' rights. A personal mandate is different from neutral advice to the whole ownership group. ENDGAME is a developing practice framework, not an empirically validated method.

sources.title: Downside and price-of-success test
sources.text: Every important move should examine both the price of success and a plausible adverse outcome. Ask what is gained, what control or flexibility is given up, what new commitments arise, what early signal would change the decision, and what alternative remains. Persist in seeking a workable goal, not in defending a contradicted route. The business owner should challenge personal assumptions as well as external dependencies. Do not create autobiographical stories to illustrate these principles.

sources.title: ENDGAME goal-based SWOT application
sources.text: Use separate owner and company SWOT perspectives referenced to an explicit objective. Internal strengths and weaknesses are distinguished from external opportunities and threats for the stated unit of analysis. Keep a shareholder and decision-rights map separate. Cross factors into strength/opportunity, weakness/opportunity, strength/threat and weakness/threat options. SWOT and TOWS are established concepts; the ENDGAME application does not invent them. Record evidence and uncertainty, check trade-offs, then test the chosen intervention.
